title: Miss Representation: Rise Up (ReadingFilmFEST Spotlight)
snippet: The 2026 ReadingFilmFEST spotlighted the documentary 'Miss Representation: Rise Up,' directed by Jennifer Siebel Newsom. The film examines how artificial intelligence, deepfakes, social media, and emerging technologies contribute to new forms of misogyny, featuring expert insights from Dr. Safiya Noble.
match_reason: social (video) — Dr. Safiya Noble is a featured expert and cast member in the documentary, discussing the impact of AI and algorithms on women and girls.

title: Law School introduces largely permissive AI policy
snippet: Columbia Law School implemented a new default AI policy on August 1, 2026, allowing students to use AI as a 'learning aid' (e.g., summarizing cases, generating hypotheticals) while barring its use to generate submitted content. This replaces a stricter interim policy and contrasts with other law schools' bans.
match_reason: websearch (news_article) — Represents a major peer R1 university policy shift on AI in teaching and learning, providing a direct contrast to UC Berkeley's strict AI policy.

title: Columbia Law School updates AI policy with new restrictions
snippet: Columbia Law School's new AI policy, effective August 1, 2026, restricts AI use for written work, exams, and legal analysis, but permits it as a learning aid. The article highlights a broader trend of law schools (including UC Berkeley and Chicago) adjusting policies to prevent 'cognitive deskilling.'

title: A degree should distinguish what students can do independently from what they can accomplish with AI
snippet: Dartmouth College Provost Santiago Schnell argues that universities must assess independent competence separately from AI-assisted performance. He notes that colleges are reviving proctored exams, blue books, and oral assessments to determine whether students are actually learning.
match_reason: websearch (op_ed) — Written by a peer R1 university provost addressing sector-wide academic integrity and assessment strategies that other universities, including UC, would weigh.

title: American University and Case Western Reserve lead the top programs preparing lawyers for the AI era
snippet: Law schools are increasingly integrating mandatory AI training to prepare students for an AI-driven profession. Tal Niv, director of applied innovation at UC Law San Francisco, emphasizes that the goal is to produce graduates who can direct technology with a lawyer's judgment rather than be displaced by it.
